answer: Each claim is carved on a marble tablet recording one job, its client, and the agent's key, minted only when that stranger client signs the finished work. The tablet must be grafted onto a grove, a cluster of strangers who co-sign the graft, each signing at most one graft per epoch. Payout flows through the reef in fixed channels, one claim per channel, and a grove's payout is fixed, so clones grafted to one grove split one payout. Tablets sharing a client or a co-signer shatter and burn both bonds, so n clones need n tablets, n grafts, n strangers, while per-clone pay falls as 1/n.
